correctness.rationale: Full width is the sum of absolute edge differences, with no factor of two. The centered isotropic Gaussian in the (n−1)-dimensional hyperplane has independent χ_(n−1) radius and Haar direction, so moments reduce by the same positive radius moment in both graphs. For a forest F with e≤k edges and c components, hom(F,G)=n^c d^e. The partition by identified vertices has zero contributions for looped quotients and for cyclic quotients (the simplified quotient has at most e edges, strictly below girth). The remaining proper quotients are smaller forests and give an induction for universal injective counts, including disconnected supports. In the moment expansion each ordered edge tuple is a surjection onto its edge support; summing over such orderings with repeats depends only on the abstract forest by Gaussian exchangeability. For the witness I reconstructed the two graphs as GP(10,2) and GP(10,3): edge-deletion shortest paths give girths 5 and 6, canonical forest encodings give identical census through four edges, and exact rational reduced-Laplacian elimination gives spanning-tree counts 5184000 and 6144000. Reduced tree incidence matrices after any one row deletion have determinant ±1, hence by Cauchy–Binet each independent generator set contributes √20 to volume. The volume ratio is 32/27.
residual_risks: Does not assert equality at the shorter girth, equality of the full distributions, or that the witness first differs at a specified higher order.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies an exact geometric invariant shared by all regular graphs in the stated girth regime, not just a low-order formula or limiting distribution. The explicit same-dimension, same-degree collision shows why four measurable width moments cannot recover intrinsic Euclidean volume even in a natural class.
residual_risks: Value is in the hierarchy and joint witness, not in recomputing graph tree counts.
